newsitem.title: USA: USWC crude prices fall as supply grows, sales thin.
newsitem.headline: USWC crude prices fall as supply grows, sales thin.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude oil prices fell Wednesday in quiet local trade, weakend by reports of rising supplies nationwide, traders said.
With imports arriving at a record rate 9.2 million a day last week, traders feared a glut at U.S refineries.
On the West Coast, negotiations were nearly finished for July purchases of local crudes, following three major buys the last few days, traders said.
With local business flat, the region's benchmark grade, Alaska North Slope (ANS), fell in sympathy with lower crude prices in other regions.
The grade's main seller, BP, offered cargoes at $1.85 under July deliveries of WTI, the U.S basis for cash and futures oil markets.

Despite falling world crude prices, discounts for ANS, have increased steadily, according to traders, with a minus $2.16 sold Monday. Higher volumes of imports, weak refinery margins out West, and a glut of buyers have weakend prices.
Outright prices for ANS were $16.64/16.84 a barrel, down 40 cents in line with WTI cash markets.
One small refiner in the U.S Northwest still needed to buy ANS and bid $2.25 under July WTI.
Heavier California grades remained unchanged near postings this week.
